title: A Duck on the Pond
standard_text:
Standard: With prompting and support, ask and answer questions about key details in a text.
 Spiral: RI.K.2 main topic · RI.K.4 unknown words · RI.K.7 illustrations · RI.K.10 group reading
 Lower range: LL 0 – 110

paras.label: A
paras.text: A duck has soft feathers under its wings.

paras.label: B
paras.text: Oil on the top feathers keeps the water out.

paras.label: C
paras.text: The soft ones under them stay dry.

paras.label: D
paras.text: So the duck stays warm all day long.

paras.label: A
paras.text: A duck has soft feathers under its wings.

paras.label: B
paras.text: Oil on top keeps the water out.

paras.label: C
paras.text: The soft ones stay dry.

paras.label: D
paras.text: The duck stays warm.

questions.q: What keeps the water out?
questions.a: Oil on the top feathers keeps the water out.

questions.q: Paragraph C (i.e. the soft feathers) and paragraph D (i.e. staying warm).
Tell what this is about.
questions.a: A duck has soft feathers under its wings. Oil on the top feathers keeps the water out, so the soft ones stay dry and the duck stays warm.

questions.q:
feathers: what covers a bird.
oil: a slippery stuff that water runs off.
Describe the connection between the oil and the duck staying warm.
questions.a: Oil on the top feathers keeps the water out, so the soft ones under them stay dry and the duck stays warm.

note: Read it twice. The second time, stop after each paragraph and ask what that one sentence told you.

title: The Crossing Light
standard_text:
Standard: With prompting and support, ask and answer questions about key details in a text.
 Spiral: RI.K.2 main topic · RI.K.4 unknown words · RI.K.7 illustrations · RI.K.10 group reading
 Lower range: LL 0 – 110

paras.label: A
paras.text: A white walking man means you may cross.

paras.label: B
paras.text: A red hand means you must wait.

paras.label: C
paras.text: The numbers count down the seconds left.

paras.label: D
paras.text: Look both ways even when the man is white.

paras.label: A
paras.text: A white man means you may cross.

paras.label: B
paras.text: A red hand means wait.

paras.label: C
paras.text: Numbers count down the seconds.

paras.label: D
paras.text: Always look both ways too.

questions.q: What does the red hand mean?
questions.a: A red hand means you must wait.

questions.q: Paragraph C (i.e. the numbers) and paragraph D (i.e. looking both ways).
Tell what the crossing light shows.
questions.a: A white walking man means you may cross and a red hand means you must wait. The numbers count down the seconds left, and you look both ways even when the man is white.

questions.q:
cross: to walk from one side to the other.
count down: to go backward, like five, four, three.
Describe the connection between the white man and looking both ways.
questions.a: You look both ways even when the man is white, because the light tells cars to stop but cannot make them.

note: Paragraph D is the one that matters most and it comes last. Say it again at the end.

title: Where a Bear Sleeps
standard_text:
Standard: With prompting and support, ask and answer questions about key details in a text.
 Spiral: RI.K.2 main topic · RI.K.4 unknown words · RI.K.7 illustrations · RI.K.10 group reading
 Lower range: LL 0 – 110

paras.label: A
paras.text: A bear finds a cave or a hole in winter.

paras.label: B
paras.text: It sleeps there for many months.

paras.label: C
paras.text: It does not eat the whole time.

paras.label: D
paras.text: In spring it comes out thin and hungry.

paras.label: A
paras.text: A bear finds a cave in winter.

paras.label: B
paras.text: It sleeps for many months.

paras.label: C
paras.text: It does not eat.

paras.label: D
paras.text: In spring it comes out hungry.

questions.q: Where does the bear sleep?
questions.a: A bear finds a cave or a hole in winter.

questions.q: Paragraph C (i.e. not eating) and paragraph D (i.e. spring).
Tell what a bear does in winter.
questions.a: A bear finds a cave or a hole, sleeps there for many months without eating, and comes out thin and hungry in spring.

questions.q:
cave: a hole in rock big enough to go into.
spring: the season that comes after winter.
Describe the connection between not eating and being hungry.
questions.a: It does not eat the whole time, so in spring it comes out thin and hungry.

note: Four paragraphs, four steps, in order. Count them on your fingers with the child.

title: The School Nurse
standard_text:
Standard: With prompting and support, ask and answer questions about key details in a text.
 Spiral: RI.K.2 main topic · RI.K.4 unknown words · RI.K.7 illustrations · RI.K.10 group reading
 Lower range: LL 0 – 110

paras.label: A
paras.text: The nurse has a small room by the office.

paras.label: B
paras.text: She keeps bandages, ice packs and a cot.

paras.label: C
paras.text: She writes down every child who comes in.

paras.label: D
paras.text: She calls home if a child needs to go.

paras.label: A
paras.text: The nurse has a room by the office.

paras.label: B
paras.text: She keeps bandages and ice packs.

paras.label: C
paras.text: She writes down who comes in.

paras.label: D
paras.text: She calls home if you need to go.

questions.q: What does the nurse keep?
questions.a: She keeps bandages, ice packs and a cot.

questions.q: Paragraph C (i.e. writing it down) and paragraph D (i.e. calling home).
Tell what the school nurse does.
questions.a: The nurse has a small room by the office with bandages, ice packs and a cot. She writes down every child who comes in, and she calls home if a child needs to go.

questions.q:
bandage: a cover that goes on a cut.
cot: a small bed you can lie down on.
Describe the connection between writing it down and calling home.
questions.a: She writes down every child who comes in, so she knows who to call home about.

note: Children know this room. Ask what they have seen in it before you read a word.

title: How a Snail Moves
standard_text:
Standard: With prompting and support, ask and answer questions about key details in a text.
 Spiral: RI.K.2 main topic · RI.K.4 unknown words · RI.K.7 illustrations · RI.K.10 group reading
 Lower range: LL 0 – 110

paras.label: A
paras.text: A snail has one wide foot under its shell.

paras.label: B
paras.text: It makes slime to slide along.

paras.label: C
paras.text: The slime lets it cross a sharp edge.

paras.label: D
paras.text: You can see the shiny trail it left.

paras.label: A
paras.text: A snail has one foot under its shell.

paras.label: B
paras.text: It makes slime to slide on.

paras.label: C
paras.text: The slime keeps it safe.

paras.label: D
paras.text: You can see its shiny trail.

questions.q: What does the snail make?
questions.a: It makes slime to slide along.

questions.q: Paragraph C (i.e. the sharp edge) and paragraph D (i.e. the trail).
Tell how a snail moves.
questions.a: A snail has one wide foot under its shell. It makes slime to slide along, the slime lets it cross a sharp edge, and you can see the shiny trail it left.

questions.q:
slime: wet slippery stuff.
trail: the mark something leaves behind.
Describe the connection between the slime and the trail.
questions.a: It makes slime to slide along, and you can see the shiny trail it left.

note: Paragraph C is the surprise: the slime is protection, not just slipperiness.

title: Winter Coats
standard_text:
Standard: With prompting and support, identify the main topic and retell key details of a text.
 Spiral: RI.K.1 key details · RI.K.3 connections · RI.K.7 illustrations · RI.K.10 group reading
 Lower range: LL 0 – 110

paras.label: A
paras.text: A dog grows thicker fur when it gets cold.

paras.label: B
paras.text: The thick fur holds warm air near the skin.

paras.label: C
paras.text: In spring the dog sheds it again.

paras.label: D
paras.text: A coat of fur comes and goes with the year.

paras.label: A
paras.text: A dog grows thicker fur when it is cold.

paras.label: B
paras.text: The fur holds warm air near the skin.

paras.label: C
paras.text: In spring the dog sheds it.

paras.label: D
paras.text: The fur comes and goes.

questions.q: What does the thick fur hold?
questions.a: The thick fur holds warm air near the skin.

questions.q: Paragraph A (i.e. growing fur) and paragraph C (i.e. shedding it).
Tell what this is about.
questions.a: A dog grows thicker fur when it gets cold, and the thick fur holds warm air near the skin. In spring the dog sheds it, so a coat of fur comes and goes with the year.

questions.q:
fur: the hair that covers an animal.
sheds: drops off.
Describe the connection between the cold and the thick fur.
questions.a: A dog grows thicker fur when it gets cold, and sheds it again in spring.

note: The topic is the whole year, not just winter. Paragraph D is what says so.

title: The Grocery Cart
standard_text:
Standard: With prompting and support, identify the main topic and retell key details of a text.
 Spiral: RI.K.1 key details · RI.K.3 connections · RI.K.7 illustrations · RI.K.10 group reading
 Lower range: LL 0 – 110

paras.label: A
paras.text: A cart has four wheels and a deep basket.

paras.label: B
paras.text: The two front wheels can turn any way.

paras.label: C
paras.text: That is how you steer around a corner.

paras.label: D
paras.text: The back wheels only roll straight.

paras.label: A
paras.text: A cart has four wheels and a basket.

paras.label: B
paras.text: The front wheels turn any way.

paras.label: C
paras.text: That is how you steer.

paras.label: D
paras.text: The back wheels roll straight.

questions.q: Which wheels can turn any way?
questions.a: The two front wheels can turn any way.

questions.q: Paragraph C (i.e. steering) and paragraph D (i.e. the back wheels).
Tell what this is about.
questions.a: A cart has four wheels and a deep basket. The two front wheels can turn any way, which is how you steer around a corner, and the back wheels only roll straight.

questions.q:
steer: to make something go the way you want.
basket: the part that holds what you put in.
Describe the connection between the front wheels and steering.
questions.a: The two front wheels can turn any way, and that is how you steer around a corner.

note: Have the child push a cart and watch the wheels. The text will make sense in one trip.

title: Seeds in the Wind
standard_text:
Standard: With prompting and support, identify the main topic and retell key details of a text.
 Spiral: RI.K.1 key details · RI.K.3 connections · RI.K.7 illustrations · RI.K.10 group reading
 Lower range: LL 0 – 110

paras.label: A
paras.text: A dandelion seed has a tiny white parachute.

paras.label: B
paras.text: The wind lifts it high off the stem.

paras.label: C
paras.text: It can land far from the plant it came from.

paras.label: D
paras.text: That is how one plant fills a whole yard.

paras.label: A
paras.text: A dandelion seed has a white top.

paras.label: B
paras.text: The wind lifts it off the stem.

paras.label: C
paras.text: It can land far away.

paras.label: D
paras.text: That is how a yard fills up.

questions.q: What lifts the seed?
questions.a: The wind lifts it high off the stem.

questions.q: Paragraph A (i.e. the parachute) and paragraph D (i.e. filling a yard).
Tell what this is about.
questions.a: A dandelion seed has a tiny white parachute. The wind lifts it high off the stem and it can land far from the plant it came from, which is how one plant fills a whole yard.

questions.q:
parachute: a soft top that catches the air.
stem: the part that holds a plant up.
Describe the connection between the parachute and landing far away.
questions.a: The seed has a tiny white parachute, so the wind lifts it high and it can land far from the plant it came from.

note: Blow a real dandelion if you can. Paragraph D is the part they will remember.

questions.a: Picture books sit on the low shelves.

title: Why Ice Floats
standard_text:
Standard: With prompting and support, identify the main topic and retell key details of a text.
 Spiral: RI.K.1 key details · RI.K.3 connections · RI.K.7 illustrations · RI.K.10 group reading
 Lower range: LL 0 – 110

paras.label: A
paras.text: Water gets bigger when it turns to ice.

paras.label: B
paras.text: A bigger piece of the same water is lighter.

paras.label: C
paras.text: So ice floats on top instead of sinking.

paras.label: D
paras.text: That is why a pond freezes from the top.

paras.label: A
paras.text: Water gets bigger when it freezes.

paras.label: B
paras.text: Bigger means lighter here.

paras.label: C
paras.text: So ice floats on top.

paras.label: D
paras.text: A pond freezes from the top down.

questions.q: What happens to water when it freezes?
questions.a: Water gets bigger when it turns to ice.

questions.q: Paragraph C (i.e. floating) and paragraph D (i.e. the pond).
Tell what this is about.
questions.a: Water gets bigger when it turns to ice, and a bigger piece of the same water is lighter. So ice floats on top instead of sinking, which is why a pond freezes from the top.

questions.q:
floats: stays up on top of the water.
freezes: turns into ice.
Describe the connection between ice being lighter and a pond freezing on top.
questions.a: A bigger piece of the same water is lighter, so ice floats on top and a pond freezes from the top down.

note: This one is hard and worth it. Put an ice cube in a glass and watch where it sits.
